anomalies.observed: The second LED of dual LED D30 has its anode A2 (D30.4) on ESTOP_OUT and its cathode K2 (D30.2) fed through R60 to ESTOP_OUT as well. The LED is therefore across the same node at both ends and cannot light. The matching channel K1 is returned to GND through R59 (130R), so the two channels are not symmetric.
anomalies.expected: The K2 current-limit resistor R60 should return to GND, as R59 does for K1, so the ESTOP_OUT indicator LED is driven between ESTOP_OUT and ground.

evidence.quote: ESTOP_OUT : D30.4(A2,input) J13.6(Pin_6,passive) J2.6(Pin_6,passive) R60.2(passive) U36.4(Y,output)

anomalies.impact: The e-stop status indicator for the ESTOP_OUT channel never lights. This removes a diagnostic cue from the e-stop loop, although the e-stop function itself is not affected.

anomalies.observed: The anodes of three status LEDs (D4, D14, D23) are on net /LED_3.3V_POWER_SW, and that net contains nothing else. No power source, switch or driver is connected to it.
anomalies.expected: The LED anode supply net should be driven from a rail, switch or driver, as the other LED anode nets are (for example /LED_3.3V_POWER_NONINV is driven by U34.4).
anomalies.impact: The Ethernet activity LEDs D14 and D23 and the power/activity LED D4 have no supply and will stay dark.

anomalies.observed: The LTC4412 SENSE pin (U6.6) is on +5V and the PMOS Q1 source (Q1.2) is on +5V. The PMOS drain (Q1.3) is on USBC_VBUS_IN, which is the VIN pin (U6.1). The MOSFET body diode therefore conducts from the +5V rail back toward VBUS.
anomalies.expected: For an LTC4412 ideal-diode stage, the PMOS source should be on the VIN (input) side and its drain on the SENSE (load) side, so that the body diode blocks reverse current.

evidence.quote: USBC_VBUS_IN [High Power] : J3.A4(VBUS,passive) J3.A9(VBUS,passive) J3.B4(VBUS,passive) J3.B9(VBUS,passive) Q1.3(D,passive) R11.1(passive) R64.2(2,passive) U25.5(VBUS,passive) U6.1(VIN,power_in)

anomalies.impact: Reverse-current protection on the USB input may not work as intended, which is the protection the spec's note says the power path was meant to provide.
